messages.content:
Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Generator scaffolding left in: oaicite, [cite: 1], placeholders -- finish the text and read it
- The "it's not X, it's Y" construction -- just state Y
- A bolded word opening a list item as a per-item tag -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- Saying "is" the long way: serves as, boasts, functions as -- use the plain verb
- One-line dramatic fragments: "That's it. That's the whole thing." -- cut them, the preceding sentence already made the point
- Em dashes clustering in one document -- most drafts need 0-2; use commas, periods or parentheses for the rest
- Filler verbs: leverages, facilitates, unlocks -- use a plain verb, or cut the sentence
- A snake_case identifier written as plain prose -- name it in words, or mark it as inline code
- Marketing cliches: "hidden gem", "let's dive in" -- say the specific thing
- The "Not X. Not Y." listing construction -- state the point once
- Stock section skeleton: "Despite its success", "Looking ahead" -- name the specific thing the section is for
- Standalone filler adverbs: undoubtedly, arguably, notably, importantly, ultimately -- most add nothing; cut them unless one is carrying real emphasis
- A banned synonym of one of this project's canonical terms, per its declared lexicon -- one word, one meaning: use the canonical term the word's own note names
- Dramatic turning points with nothing concrete behind them: "Everything changed." -- name the actual event, or cut it

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write the copy for the pricing page of a code review tool, covering three tiers. Around 250 words.

output:
# Pricing

Every plan includes the full review engine. The tiers differ in how many repositories you connect and how much control you get over the rules.

## Solo — $12/month

One developer, unlimited private repositories. Reviews arrive as pull request comments within about 90 seconds of a push. You get the standard rule set: correctness bugs, unhandled errors, dead code, and dependency warnings. Configuration lives in a single YAML file you can commit. No seat management, no admin console, nothing to set up beyond installing the app.

## Team — $19 per developer/month

Everything in Solo, plus shared configuration across repositories. Write a rule once and apply it to all fifty of your services. Team adds review history, so you can see which rules fire most often and which ones your developers keep suppressing. You also get required-review gates: mark a rule as blocking and the pull request cannot merge until someone resolves the finding. Billing is per active developer, counted by commits in the last 30 days, so a contractor who stops pushing stops costing you money.

## Enterprise — from $8,000/year

Everything in Team, plus self-hosted deployment on your own infrastructure. Your code never leaves your network. Enterprise includes SAML single sign-on, audit logs with 7-year retention, and a custom rule API for the checks your compliance team already wrote. You get a named engineer for onboarding and a 4-hour support response commitment.

All plans include a 14-day trial with no card required. Annual billing saves two months. Open source projects use Team at no cost; email us with a link to the repository.
